競.meaning: Twin boys argue over which one is the <part>big brother</part>. Each climbs onto a box to <part>stand</part> taller, then onto a ladder, then up onto the chimney. Mum sighs from the garden: they turn everything into a race. They always <kanji>compete</kanji>.
競.on: Their prize is one shiny front door <sound>key</sound>, and the winner yells '<sound>Oh</sound>!' so fast the two sounds squash together.
競.kun: They even race to peel a <sound>ki</sound>wi and pull on a <sound>so</sound>ck.

浮.meaning: A <part>stork</part> forgets how to fly, so it lies on its back on the pond, wings out, and lets the <part>water drops</part> carry it along. Fish swim underneath, ducks climb aboard like it's a raft. It isn't swimming at all, just <kanji>floating</kanji>.
浮.on: It says the pond is as comfy as a rolled-out <sound>fu</sound>ton.
浮.kun: A frog rides on its tummy, slurping a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don.

村.meaning: A family of hedgehogs lives in one hollow <part>tree</part>. Every morning they tee off from the roots with a tiny <part>golf club</part>, and wherever the acorn lands, they build a new hut. After a year there are fifty huts: a whole <kanji>village</kanji>.
村.on: Their mayor wears a <sound>som</sound>brero made from one big leaf.
村.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se wanders in and asks for a hut too, and the hedgehogs cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

囲.meaning: A frog at the bottom of a <part>well</part> looks up and sees a <part>cage</part> being lowered over the top, then a ring of curious ducks around the cage, then a ring of goats around the ducks. Everyone wants a look. Rings and rings of them <kanji>surround</kanji> it.
囲.on: Down in the water, an <sound>ee</sound>l coils round the frog as well.
囲.kun: Then a <sound>ca</sound>rt full of <sound>koa</sound>las rolls up and joins the ring.

節.meaning: A wizard can grow <part>bamboo</part> in an <part>instant</part>: zap, a stalk shoots up. But it grows in jerks, stop, start, stop, and each stop leaves a hard little ring round the stem. Count the rings to know how many spells. Each ring is a <kanji>node</kanji>.
節.on: A red <sound>set</sound>ter sniffs every ring and barks once at each.
節.kun: Then the wizard curls up on a <sound>fu</sound>ton stuffed with <sound>shee</sound>p's wool.

植.meaning: A robot gardener lowers a baby <part>tree</part> into a hole, then checks it with a laser ten times to be sure it stands perfectly <part>straight</part>. One wobble and it pulls it out and starts again. Six hours later the robot finally manages to <kanji>plant</kanji> it.
植.on: Then it waters the soil and gets an electric <sound>shock</sound>.
植.kun: To help the tree grow, it plays it a little song on the <sound>u</sound>kulele.

況.meaning: <part>Big brother</part> is babysitting, and the bath overflows: <part>water drops</part> on the stairs, toys floating down the hall, the cat paddling past. Mum phones: 'How's the house?' He looks around. 'The <kanji>condition</kanji> is... wet.'
況.on: He hides the front door <sound>key</sound> under a floating duck and gasps '<sound>Oh</sound>!' in one quick squeak as her car pulls up.
況.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>'s home, and she hasn't even seen the <sound>shee</sound>ts yet, let alone the cat.

借.meaning: You hang your coat on a <part>coat hook</part> in a museum of <part>antiquity</part>. When you come back, it's gone: an old marble statue is wearing it. Next day it's back on the hook with a thank-you note in old Latin. The statue only wanted to <kanji>borrow</kanji> it.
借.on: The note is signed with a tiny drawing of a <sound>sha</sound>rk.
借.kun: The next week, the statue asks for the keys to your <sound>ca</sound>r.

駆.meaning: A <part>horse</part> takes the night shift as a taxi in the busiest <part>ward</part> of the city. Passengers hop on its back, and it thunders down the high street, round buses and past the flower stalls. It never stops for anything: watch it <kanji>drive</kanji>.
駆.on: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo rides on its head, calling out the stops.
駆.kun: <sound>Ca</sound>rs pull over to the side to let it gallop past.

劇.meaning: At the zoo's talent night, a <part>tiger</part> and a <part>pig</part> put on a play. The pig waves a rubber <part>dagger</part>, the tiger faints, the pig weeps, the tiger sits up for a bow. The penguins sob into their flippers. What a <kanji>drama</kanji>.
劇.on: The whole show is directed by a <sound>gec</sound>ko in a beret, clinging to the curtain.

企.meaning: At the bus <part>stop</part>, a girl opens her <part>umbrella</part> and announces she'll sell umbrellas to everyone waiting in the rain. By the next bus she's sold forty and hired her grandad. That's a bold business to <kanji>undertake</kanji>.
企.on: She keeps the cash in a tin locked with a big brass <sound>key</sound>.
企.kun: Her grandad's <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock squawks '<sound>Wah</sound>!' while she draws the next plan on a <sound>da</sound>rtboard.

協.meaning: A whale is stuck on the beach. <part>Ten</part> <part>strongmen</part> grab a rope each, count to three and heave together: one grunt, one pull, and it slides back into the sea. Nobody could have done it alone. It takes <kanji>cooperation</kanji>.
協.on: The whale thanks them with a <sound>key</sound> to its sea cave, and they all say '<sound>Oh</sound>!' in one quick squeak.

験.meaning: At a <part>campsite</part>, a <part>horse</part> is the safety inspector. It kicks every tent peg, leans on every pole and sniffs every sausage. Only tents that survive get a gold rosette. It's very strict <kanji>verification</kanji>.
験.on: Then it checks the <sound>ken</sound>nel by the gate, where the camp dog barks at it.
験.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' says the horse, and stamps a <sound>ca</sound>rd and a <sound>shee</sound>t of paper as proof.

核.meaning: Deep in the trunk of an old <part>tree</part>, a tiny <part>acrobat</part> spins on a trapeze, and the whole tree swirls around her: sap, rings, bark, all turning. Saw the trunk in half and there she is at the very centre: the <kanji>nucleus</kanji>.
核.on: Beside her lies a fish <sound>carc</sound>ass that a squirrel hid there long ago.

恐.meaning: A completely <part>commonplace</part> stool sits on the <part>workbench</part>. Nothing odd about it, except it creaked at midnight. The carpenter's <part>heart</part> pounds; he hides under a blanket and won't go near it. Pure <kanji>fear</kanji>.
恐.on: In the morning he finds a mouse with a <sound>key</sound> in its paws, and squeaks '<sound>Oh</sound>!' so fast the two run together.
恐.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter peeks out from behind the <sound>so</sound>fa, just as scared as he is.

否.meaning: A parrot's <part>mouth</part> is stuck on one <part>negative</part> word. Offer a cracker: 'No.' Open the cage: 'No.' Ask if it's a parrot: 'No.' Whatever you say, it will <kanji>negate</kanji> it.
否.on: It stamps its claw in a doll's high <sound>hee</sound>l and says no again.
否.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>w, <sound>nah</sound>,' it squawks at the cracker, turning its beak away.

健.meaning: At ninety-nine, a grandpa hangs his walking stick on the <part>coat hook</part> for good and sets out to <part>build</part> his own treehouse. He hauls planks, swings a hammer, sings while he works and never catches a cold. He's terribly <kanji>healthy</kanji>.
健.on: He builds his dog a <sound>ken</sound>nel too, with a little running track.
健.kun: He scrubs the <sound>soo</sound>t off the chimney with a <sound>koa</sound>la on his shoulder.

筆.meaning: A lighthouse keeper ties a fat <part>brush</part> to a long <part>bamboo</part> pole, dips it in the sea and paints huge letters across the clouds: HELLO, SHIPS. Sailors can read it for miles. That's some <kanji>writing</kanji>.
筆.on: A <sound>hitch</sound>hiker on the cliff reads it and sticks out his thumb at a passing boat.
筆.kun: Afterwards the keeper naps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton out on the <sound>de</sound>ck, brush in hand.

探.meaning: A lost sailor is sure his treasure chest is somewhere in the woods. He drags his ship's <part>anchor</part> along the ground, throws a fishing <part>net</part> over every <part>tree</part>, and shakes out squirrels, kites and one grumpy owl. No chest yet. The <kanji>search</kanji> goes on.
探.on: Next he digs a long <sound>tun</sound>nel under the roots.
探.kun: In the dark he finds a <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin, still <sound>goo</sound>d to eat, and keeps groping about.

吸.meaning: A tired lifeguard sits by the pool with a <part>catch net</part> for leaves, but it's far too slow. So he opens his <part>mouth</part> wide and slurps: leaves, a rubber duck, two goggles and half the water. He can really <kanji>suck</kanji>.
吸.on: Out pops a pool <sound>cue</sound> that someone dropped in last summer.
吸.kun: Then he slurps the <sound>soo</sound>t off the chimney next door.

衛.meaning: At the busiest <part>crossroads</part> in the land, a tall <part>pagoda</part> stands guard. Its monks keep buckets of custard on every tier and tip them over any army that marches through. Not one has got past. It's the kingdom's best <kanji>defense</kanji>.
衛.on: Squirrels on the roof drop one hard <sound>a</sound>corn each on the soldiers' helmets.

即.meaning: A <part>robot</part> clerk has a rubber <part>stamp</part> for a hand. Slap, slap: every form is approved before you've finished your sentence. Passport? Done. Fishing licence? Done. Results in an <kanji>instant</kanji>.
即.on: It even stamps the <sound>sock</sound> you drop on its desk.
即.kun: It stamps the <sound>soo</sound>t on your hand, your <sound>na</sound>an bread and your baby's '<sound>Wah</sound>!': that is to say, everything.

季.meaning: A <part>child</part> plants one stalk of <part>grain</part> and sits beside it with a stopwatch. Green, then gold, then cut, then snow, then green again: she times each one and writes it in her notebook. She's timing the <kanji>seasons</kanji>.
季.on: Every year she locks the notebook with the same brass <sound>key</sound>.

査.meaning: A detective squirrel climbs a <part>tree</part> with a magnifying glass. 'Footprints on this branch,' she notes, 'and <part>moreover</part>, crumbs. And moreover, a sock.' The list goes on and on. She loves to <kanji>investigate</kanji>.
査.on: The crumbs lead to a half-eaten <sound>sa</sound>rdine in a hollow.

典.meaning: In an old kingdom every law is written as a <part>melody</part>, and <part>eight</part> monks carry the giant songbook on their shoulders. Break a rule and they sing it at you, very loudly, until you say sorry. It's the kingdom's <kanji>code</kanji>.
典.on: The loudest is a <sound>ten</sound>or who hits the top note on 'no parking'.
典.kun: Their next warning is pinned to your <sound>fu</sound>ton: '<sound>Mee</sound>t us at dawn.' A letter.

辞.meaning: A food critic touches one <part>chili</part> to the tip of his <part>tongue</part>. His face goes red, his ears whistle, smoke pours out from under his hat. He writes one line on a napkin, 'I quit', and hands it to his boss. He has decided to <kanji>resign</kanji>.
辞.on: He drives off into the sunset in an open <sound>jee</sound>p, tongue flapping in the wind.
辞.kun: Then he sells all his forks at a <sound>ya</sound>rd sale, done with food for good.

著.meaning: <part>Someone</part> has written a book about <part>grass</part>, just grass, nine hundred pages of it. To everyone's surprise it sells millions. Now crowds follow her through every park, asking her to sign their lawns. She's <kanji>renowned</kanji>.
著.on: She arrives at signings by <sound>cho</sound>pper, blowing everyone's hair flat.
著.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>! <sound>Rah</sound>! <sound>Wah</sound>!' her fans gasp, cheer and sob as she says she'll publish a second book.

志.meaning: A tiny <part>gentleman</part> in a top hat stands on a giant <part>heart</part> and steers it like a ship with his umbrella: 'Left! To the cake shop!' The heart wobbles down the street toward the bakery. He knows exactly what he means to do: that's his <kanji>intention</kanji>.
志.on: Bumping into lampposts on the way, he holds up a <sound>shi</sound>eld.
志.kun: He steers past a <sound>koa</sound>la on a <sound>co</sound>t, round a <sound>ro</sound>ck, and into the ba<sound>za</sound>ar he's aiming for.

程.meaning: At the fair, a farmer stacks her <part>grain</part> on the <part>display</part> table, sack on sack, until it pokes through the roof of the tent. The judges don't know where to start. They climb a ladder to measure the <kanji>extent</kanji> of it.
程.on: They measure it with a roll of <sound>ta</sound>pe that runs out halfway up.
程.kun: The prize is a <sound>ho</sound>t pie and a toy <sound>do</sound>lphin, each about this big.

跡.meaning: A <part>jellyfish</part> borrows a boot for one <part>foot</part> and goes for a stroll along the beach. Behind it trails a line of single boot prints and a squiggly slime line. Next morning, detectives scratch their heads over the <kanji>tracks</kanji>.
跡.on: They draw a map and colour in each <sound>sec</sound>tor where the prints turn up.
跡.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' A crab spots the trail and follows it to the <sound>to</sound>p of the dunes.
